artifacts.summary: Evidence and recommended rulings for amending R1-R3 and R5 to per-batch worktree side branches with per-task attribution landing; reproduces D1/D2/D4 and the surviving wrong-root defect, rejects the symlink candidate, rules Lean repositories to opt-out.

user_decision.question: In a repository where specs/ is tracked, may task-bookkeeping commits (research, plan, phase-marker, state) keep landing directly on the integration branch between the per-task squash commits, or must each task's state and artifact changes be held uncommitted and folded into its single squash commit?
options: Bookkeeping commits land directly on the integration branch, as today; the squash commit carries code only
Hold each task's specs/ changes uncommitted in the primary tree and fold them into the task's squash commit
user_decision.recommended: Bookkeeping commits land directly on the integration branch, as today; the squash commit carries code only

claim_invalidations.claim: milestone-ref-land.sh --verify's ancestry assertion cannot hold after the first landing: a three-landing replay of the script's own primitives passes once and fails twice while tree equality passes all three times and fails on a deliberately unlanded commit.
specs/ is tracked in this repository (git check-ignore matches only /.claude/), so a fresh worktree carries a HEAD-stale specs/ copy and the symlink candidate cannot apply to it.

memory_candidates.content: A directory-only gitignore pattern (trailing slash, e.g. /.claude/ or /specs/) does not match a symlink of the same name: the link shows as untracked, dirties the tree and blocks `git worktree remove`. A slashless pattern in the shared $GIT_COMMON_DIR/info/exclude covers it for every worktree. Separately, `git worktree remove` without --force refuses on modified and untracked files but NOT on ignored files, which it deletes silently.

To land one task's work from a branch shared by interleaved tasks, `git merge --squash <end commit>` co-lands sibling commits; select the task's commits by subject and `git cherry-pick -n` them, then commit once. Verify by blob equality over the task's own path set (full-tree equality breaks once the target carries anything else). A squash-landed branch is refused by `git branch -d`; `git update-ref -d <ref> <proven-tip>` deletes it by compare-and-swap, so a branch that advanced after its proof cannot be deleted.

guard-destructive-git.sh decides dirtiness with `git status --porcelain` in the hook's own process directory and does not parse `cd` or `git -C` in the command text, so commands aimed at another repository or worktree are judged by the session tree's state: blocked when the session tree is dirty, allowed when it is clean. Scratch-fixture git experiments must avoid whole-tree staging and working-tree discard verbs for this reason.
